hints: Focus on the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs around the central atom, since lone pairs repel more strongly and squeeze bond angles smaller.
Work out the shapes first: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ is trigonal planar at each carbon, while $\text{NH}_4^+$ is perfectly tetrahedral with no lone pair.
Compare the tetrahedral species with the one that has a lone pair as well, and remember how that extra repulsion changes $109.5^\circ$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the VSEPR rule for bond angles**

Think of electron pairs pushing each other apart. The order of repulsion is lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair.

So more lone pairs means a smaller bond angle:
$$\text{trigonal planar } 120^\circ > \text{tetrahedral } 109.5^\circ > \text{pyramidal with lone pair } \approx 107^\circ$$

**Find the shape and angle for each species**

Let's look at each one side by side.

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$: Each C has 3 bonding regions and no lone pair, trigonal planar, angle $\approx 120^\circ$.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$: The $\text{CH}_3$ carbons are tetrahedral ($\approx 109.5^\circ$) and the $\text{C=O}$ carbon is trigonal planar ($\approx 120^\circ$). Smallest here is $109.5^\circ$.

$\text{NH}_4^+$: N has 4 bonding pairs and no lone pair, perfect tetrahedral, angle $= 109.5^\circ$.

$\text{NH}_3$: N has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, trigonal pyramidal, angle squeezed to $\approx 107^\circ$.

**Pick the smallest**

Comparing the smallest angle in each: $120^\circ$, $109.5^\circ$, $109.5^\circ$, and $107^\circ$.

The lone pair in ammonia pushes the N-H bonds closer together, so it has the smallest bond angle of the four.

options.A: Incorrect. In $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ each carbon is trigonal planar with 3 bond pairs and no lone pair, giving H-C-H and H-C-C angles of about $120^\circ$. This is the largest angle here, not the smallest.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ contains both tetrahedral carbons ($\approx 109.5^\circ$) and a trigonal planar carbonyl carbon ($\approx 120^\circ$). Its smallest angle is $109.5^\circ$, which is still larger than the lone pair squeezed angle in ammonia.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_4^+$ has 4 bonding pairs and zero lone pairs on nitrogen, so it is a regular tetrahedron with angle $109.5^\circ$. Students often confuse it with $\text{NH}_3$, but without a lone pair there is no extra squeezing.
options.D: Correct. $\text{NH}_3$ has 3 bonding pairs plus 1 lone pair on nitrogen, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape. The lone pair-bond pair repulsion squeezes the H-N-H angle from $109.5^\circ$ down to about $107^\circ$, the smallest of the four.
